title: Charge on the Gel, Grease in the Cell
endLine: Charge explains the gel; polarity explains the sickle.

scenes.tts: The first film ended on a gel, with sickle hemoglobin trailing normal hemoglobin. But a slower drift in a gel cannot bend a red cell. So what does that one valine actually do?
scenes.narration: The first film ended on a gel, with sickle hemoglobin trailing normal hemoglobin. But a slower drift in a gel cannot bend a red cell. So what does that one valine actually do?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset. COLOUR MAP, as before: proton = GOLD token; acid-type switch = ORANGE; base-type switch = BLUE; net charge = TEAL; text and pole labels = WHITE. New in this film: greasy (hydrophobic) = OLIVE; water = pale CYAN specks; red blood cell = CRIMSON. ONE WORLD for the whole film: a pale CYAN water bath of slowly drifting specks fills the frame; a horizontal gel strip runs across the top quarter, '−' at its left end and '+' at its right, exactly as the first film left it; the main stage below holds one large rounded blob, 'sickle hemoglobin' (fills about 60% of frame height), tagged 'schematic'. Open on the first film's last picture: two blobs, 'normal hemoglobin' and 'sickle hemoglobin', drifting right along the strip toward '+', the sickle one lagging. On 'cannot bend a red cell' a large round CRIMSON red cell fades in on the main stage, and a faint crescent outline flickers over it and fades. On 'that one valine' an OLIVE chip labelled 'valine' pulses on the sickle blob in the strip, and a white '?' appears beside the red cell.
Title card, 2 s: 'Charge on the Gel, Grease in the Cell'. Behind it the two blobs keep drifting along the gel strip and CYAN water specks keep moving.

scenes.tts: Start with what the gel saw. Glutamate's side chain is an acid switch, and at blood p H it has let go: minus one. Valine has no switch at all, so it carries nothing.
scenes.narration: Start with what the gel saw. Glutamate's side chain is an acid switch, and at blood pH it has let go: −1. Valine has no switch at all, so it carries nothing.
scenes.caption: Start with what the gel saw. Glutamate's side chain is an acid switch, and at blood pH it has let go: −1. Valine has no switch at all, so it carries nothing.
scenes.visual: The red cell fades; the camera eases onto the main stage, where the large hemoglobin blob sits in the water. Two side-chain sockets on its upper surface are marked 'position 6', one per beta chain (label 'beta chain' under each). On 'Glutamate's' each socket holds an ORANGE acid-type switch labelled 'glutamate'; its GOLD token lifts off and floats away, and a badge '−1' appears. On 'Valine' both ORANGE switches morph into plain OLIVE chips labelled 'valine', badge '0', with a small tag 'no switch'. CYAN specks keep drifting past.

scenes.tts: Hemoglobin has two beta chains, so the swap removes two negative charges per molecule. In an alkaline buffer, every hemoglobin is net negative and drifts toward the positive pole. Sickle hemoglobin, two charges less negative, falls behind.
scenes.narration: Hemoglobin has two beta chains, so the swap removes two negative charges per molecule. In an alkaline buffer, every hemoglobin is net negative and drifts toward the positive pole. Sickle hemoglobin, two charges less negative, falls behind.
scenes.visual: On 'two beta chains' both '−1' badges (shown as ghosts beside the OLIVE chips) slide off the blob and into a TEAL readout at the blob's right: 'change: +2 per molecule'. On 'alkaline buffer' the camera tilts up to the gel strip; a white label 'alkaline buffer' appears above it and both blobs on the strip show a TEAL '−' badge. On 'positive pole' the '+' end glows and gets the label 'anode (+)'. On 'falls behind' both blobs drift right; the normal blob pulls ahead and the sickle blob, its TEAL badge smaller, lags (relative positions schematic).

scenes.tts: But a side chain has a second property: polarity, how comfortable it is in water. Glutamate is charged and hydrophilic, at ease in water. Valine is a greasy hydrocarbon chain. It is hydrophobic.
scenes.narration: But a side chain has a second property: polarity, how comfortable it is in water. Glutamate is charged and hydrophilic, at ease in water. Valine is a greasy hydrocarbon chain. It is hydrophobic.
scenes.visual: Camera returns to the main stage. The CYAN water specks become the subject: they drift right up to the blob's surface. On 'polarity' a large white word 'polarity' writes above the blob. On 'Glutamate' a ghost ORANGE glutamate switch reappears beside one socket; CYAN specks cluster snugly round it; label 'hydrophilic'. On 'Valine' the OLIVE chip glows; the CYAN specks around it pull back and leave a clear gap, as oil leaves a gap in water; label 'hydrophobic'. The ghost glutamate fades.

scenes.tts: In a protein that dissolves in water, greasy side chains tend to be buried in the core. There they stay away from water. Charged and polar side chains tend to face the water outside.
scenes.narration: In a protein that dissolves in water, greasy side chains tend to be buried in the core. There they stay away from water. Charged and polar side chains tend to face the water outside.
scenes.visual: The blob turns semi-transparent to show its inside, tagged 'schematic'. On 'buried in the core' a cluster of OLIVE tokens settles into the blob's centre, label 'greasy core'; no CYAN specks enter. On 'face the water' a ring of ORANGE and BLUE switch tokens and small white 'polar' tokens lines the outer edge, label 'water-facing surface', with CYAN specks drifting against them. The blob's outline then closes again.

scenes.tts: Position six of each beta chain sits on the surface, facing water, where glutamate is at home. Swap in valine, and a greasy patch now sits out in the water.
scenes.narration: Position six of each beta chain sits on the surface, facing water, where glutamate is at home. Swap in valine, and a greasy patch now sits out in the water.
scenes.visual: The two 'position 6' sockets on the outer edge brighten; for a moment each again holds a ghost ORANGE glutamate with CYAN specks snug around it. On 'Swap in valine' the ghosts morph back into the OLIVE valine chips, each a separate greasy patch on its own side of the molecule; the nearer one brightens, label 'greasy patch'. The CYAN specks pull away from each patch and leave a visible empty halo in the water around each, while specks still hug the rest of the surface.

scenes.tts: So one swap changed two properties at once. Here is the whole idea. Charge explains how the defect was first seen. Polarity explains why the cells sickle.
scenes.narration: So one swap changed two properties at once. Here is the whole idea. Charge explains how the defect was first seen. Polarity explains why the cells sickle.
scenes.visual: Split the frame softly without a reset: the gel strip slides down to the left half (two blobs, sickle one lagging), and the hemoglobin blob with its OLIVE patch shrinks to the right half. On 'two properties' two large labels appear: TEAL 'charge' over the gel, OLIVE 'polarity' over the blob. On 'Charge explains' the gel's blobs drift once more and the TEAL label glows. On 'Polarity explains' the OLIVE patch glows and a CRIMSON red-cell outline, round, fades in behind the blob with a white '?' on it.

scenes.tts: Now watch what happens when hemoglobin gives up its oxygen. Its shape shifts. A matching hydrophobic pocket opens on its surface, greasy like the patch.
scenes.narration: Now watch what happens when hemoglobin gives up its oxygen. Its shape shifts. A matching hydrophobic pocket opens on its surface, greasy like the patch.
scenes.caption: Now watch what happens when hemoglobin gives up its oxygen. Its shape shifts. A matching hydrophobic pocket opens on its surface, greasy like the patch.
scenes.visual: The gel strip shrinks to a small thumbnail in the top-left corner and stays there for the rest of the film. The hemoglobin blob returns to full size. On 'gives up its oxygen' four small white 'O2' dots leave the blob and drift off; label 'oxygen leaves'. On 'shape shifts' the blob's outline slowly bulges and reshapes. On 'pocket opens' a dent opens on the blob's opposite side, lined in OLIVE, label 'greasy pocket'; CYAN specks pull back from it too.

scenes.tts: Picture two of these molecules side by side. One carries a greasy patch. The next has a greasy pocket. Neither is comfortable in water. What happens when they meet?
scenes.narration: Picture two of these molecules side by side. One carries a greasy patch. The next has a greasy pocket. Neither is comfortable in water. What happens when they meet?
scenes.visual: A second identical blob (patch and pocket both shown) slides in from the right; the two now sit side by side, the first one's OLIVE patch facing the second one's OLIVE pocket across a gap of CYAN water. On 'greasy patch' the first blob's patch pulses; on 'greasy pocket' the second blob's pocket pulses. On 'What happens' a question card writes across the top: 'Patch meets pocket: what happens?'
Thinking pause: the question card stays. The two blobs bob gently in place; the patch and pocket pulse slowly in turn; CYAN specks keep drifting through the gap between them.

scenes.tts: The valine patch of one molecule sticks into the pocket on the next. That one's patch docks into the next pocket, and so on. Hemoglobin chains into long, rigid fibers.
scenes.narration: The valine patch of one molecule sticks into the pocket on the next. That one's patch docks into the next pocket, and so on. Hemoglobin chains into long, rigid fibers.
scenes.visual: The question card fades. On 'sticks into' the first blob's OLIVE patch slides across the gap and seats in the second blob's pocket; the CYAN water between them is squeezed out. On 'and so on' a third, fourth and fifth blob slide in from the right and each docks patch-into-pocket, building a chain that runs across the frame. On 'long, rigid fibers' the camera pulls back: several such chains line up side by side into a straight, stiff bundle, label 'rigid fiber (schematic)'. At most 6 labelled things on screen.

scenes.tts: These rigid fibers deform the red cell into a sickle. That is where the disease starts. Hemolysis, inflammation and blocked vessels follow from it.
scenes.narration: These rigid fibers deform the red cell into a sickle. That is where the disease starts. Hemolysis, inflammation and blocked vessels follow from it.
scenes.visual: Pull back further: the CRIMSON red cell fades in round the fiber bundles, which lie inside it. On 'deform' the bundles lengthen and the round cell bends slowly into a crescent, label 'sickled red cell'. On 'Hemolysis, inflammation and blocked vessels' three small white labels appear in turn beside the crescent: 'hemolysis', 'inflammation', 'blocked vessels', each with a short arrow from the cell.

scenes.tts: So read each side chain twice: once for its charge, once for its comfort in water. The gel counted the lost negative charges. The red cell felt the new grease.
scenes.narration: So read each side chain twice: once for its charge, once for its comfort in water. The gel counted the lost negative charges. The red cell felt the new grease.
scenes.visual: The three labels fade. The gel thumbnail in the top-left corner grows back to half the frame on the left, beside the crescent cell on the right. On 'its charge' a TEAL badge pulses on the OLIVE valine chip ('0', no switch); on 'comfort in water' the OLIVE patch pulses and its CYAN halo shimmers. On 'The gel counted' the two blobs on the strip drift, the sickle one lagging. On 'felt the new grease' the fibers inside the crescent glow OLIVE.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (gel blobs drifting at left, CYAN water specks, the crescent CRIMSON cell at right). Large white text, centred: 'Charge explains the gel; polarity explains the sickle.'
